skills.description:
Skill libraries served on demand (dirs containing `<skill>/SKILL.md`).
Skills here cost ZERO session context until read_skill fetches them.

call_timeout_secs.description: Seconds allowed for a proxied tool call.

startup_timeout_secs.description: Seconds allowed for a backend to start + initialize.

refresh_on_start.description: Refresh the tool snapshot at startup when the config changed.

health_check_secs.description:
How often to check if warm backends are still alive (seconds).
0 = disabled. When a dead connection is detected, it is reset
so the next execute reconnects fresh.

inherit_env.description:
Give backends geco's whole environment.

Default false: a backend starts from a clean environment containing
only the OS/runtime baseline (see `env_passthrough`), whatever its
`env` and `pass_env` declare, and nothing else. That way a
`GITHUB_TOKEN` exported in your shell for one server isn't handed to
every other server you run. Set true to let every backend inherit
everything.

refresh_concurrency.description:
How many backends may be probed at once during a snapshot refresh.

A refresh spawns every configured server to ask for its tool list. With
no cap, twenty `npx` backends means twenty node processes starting at
the same instant — a memory and CPU spike right at agent startup, which
is the worst possible moment for it. 0 means unlimited.

env_passthrough.description:
Extra variables to pass through to every backend when isolating,
as glob patterns (`*` wildcard), e.g. `["NODE_*", "DOCKER_HOST"]`.

The built-in baseline already covers OS essentials, locale, TLS trust
and proxy settings — this is for tool-specific configuration that
isn't a secret. Per-server needs belong in `pass_env` instead.
Ignored when `inherit_env` is true. Matched case-insensitively on
Windows, where environment names are case-insensitive.

search_synonyms.description:
Extra synonym groups for tool and skill search — the escape hatch for
the case geco's lexical ranking cannot reach on its own: when your
users describe a goal in words the tool's name and description never
use. Each inner list is a set of interchangeable words, e.g.
`[["k8s", "kubernetes"], ["repo", "repository"]]`. Words are matched
after the same stemming queries and tools get, so write them plainly.
Applied on top of the built-in table; picked up on config hot-reload.

picker.description:
Optional LLM-backed tool picker. Lexical ranking finds the right tool
first only ~13% of the time when the request shares no vocabulary with
it; handing BM25F's candidates to a real model and asking which one the
user meant measured 3x better (see docs/search-ranking.md). Off by
default — it costs a round-trip per search.

surface.description:
How many meta-tools to advertise: `lean` (default) or `full`.

`lean` serves `search`, `execute` and `read_skill` — the last only when
a skill library is configured, so a plain setup is two tools. `full`
adds `list_mcp_servers`, `list_tools` and `list_skills`, which cost
~1 KB of always-on context, about a quarter of the surface.

The default is lean because everything those three do is reachable
without them, and reachable ON DEMAND rather than in every request —
which is the argument geco makes about backend schemas, applied to its
own surface:

- browsing what exists → `search("*")`, one entry per server with a
  tool count and a five-name preview, and `search("*", kind="skills")`
  for the library
- a tool's input schema → `search(include_schema=true)`
- gateway problems → the `issues` key, which rides on every `search`
  response that needs it

Crucially a miss does not depend on the model knowing any of that: a
search that matches nothing volunteers the server list in its hint,
automatically, which is the recovery path browsing used to serve.

Set `full` if you want the browse tools back. The one thing lean
genuinely loses is enumerating a single server's whole tool list —
`search("*")` previews five names each, and `geco inspect` has the rest
for a human.

PickerConfig.description:
How (and whether) to ask a language model which candidate tool a request
means. Transports are tried in preference order and any failure falls back
to plain lexical ranking, so enabling this can only add latency, never
break search.

mode.description:
`off` (default), `auto`, `sampling`, or `command`.

`auto` prefers MCP sampling when the connected client advertises the
capability (no config, uses the client's own model), then `command`.
Anything configured but unavailable degrades to lexical ranking rather
than failing the search.

command.description:
Command to run, e.g. `["~/.config/geco/picker/pick.sh", "{prompt}"]`
— the wrapper the installer scaffolds, which discovers your harness's
current model and calls it.

`{prompt}` anywhere in the arguments is replaced by the prompt; with no
placeholder it is appended as the final argument. A leading `~/` in the
program is expanded; arguments are passed through untouched, since one
of them is the user's own query. The child sees `GECO_NO_PICKER=1` and,
when a client has handshaken, `GECO_CLIENT` with its name. Reach an
OpenAI-compatible endpoint with a small wrapper script — geco ships no
HTTP client, deliberately.

candidates.description:
How many BM25F candidates to hand the model when the whole catalogue
does NOT fit in `whole_catalogue_tokens`. Above that threshold this is
the fallback, not the normal path.

whole_catalogue_tokens.description:
When the entire tool catalogue fits in roughly this many tokens, hand
the model ALL of it and skip lexical retrieval for candidate selection
entirely. `0` disables, always using `candidates`.

This is the single biggest measured win in the whole search story, and
it works for a reason that inverts the usual intuition about retrieval.
On a realistic 8-server catalogue (324 tools), same model and prompt:

| candidates | recall ceiling | rank-1 |
|---|---|---|
| BM25F top-50 | 82% | 74.6% |
| every tool that scores | 91% | 78.5% |
| **the whole catalogue** | **100%** | **94.8%** |

Precision did not fall under 7x the distractors — 90.5% against the
shortlist's 90.7%, measured like for like, with the last 4 points
coming from putting the catalogue before the question rather than
after it. **BM25F does not select random distractors — it selects the
most confusable ones.** Every shortlisted candidate was chosen for
sharing vocabulary with the query, so the shortlist is precisely the
set of plausible wrong answers, while the tools it discards are mostly
obvious non-answers a model rejects at a glance.

It is also FASTER, because the catalogue is then a stable prompt
prefix: measured 0.9s against 2.2s for top-50, with 96.6% of the
prompt served from cache.

The estimate is characters/4 and deliberately rough — it decides
between two working modes, not whether a request succeeds.

timeout_secs.description: Seconds to wait before giving up and returning the lexical order.

absorb.description:
Directories SWEPT into `dirs[0]` at startup and on refresh: any
skill (subdir with SKILL.md) found here is MOVED into the library.
Point this at your agent's native auto-loaded skills dir to enforce
"nothing is ever native" — wherever a model drops a skill, the
gateway absorbs it. Name collisions are skipped and reported.

description.description:
One-line description shown in `list_mcp_servers`. Optional but worth
writing: it is the only thing the agent sees before drilling in.

allow.description: Tool allowlist (glob, `*` wildcard). Empty = every tool.

deny.description: Tool denylist (glob). Deny wins over allow.

pass_env.description:
Environment variables to forward from the proxy's own environment
to THIS backend at spawn time, e.g. `pass_env: ["GITHUB_TOKEN"]`.

Backends do not inherit geco's environment, so this is how a server
gets an ambient secret — and only the servers that list it do.
Missing variables are skipped silently, which is the right behaviour
for optional ones; use `env` to fail loudly instead.

call_timeout_secs.description:
Override `proxy.call_timeout_secs` for this server only.
For the one backend that is legitimately slow, instead of loosening
the bound for every other server too.

startup_timeout_secs.description:
Override `proxy.startup_timeout_secs` for this server only — e.g. a
backend whose first run downloads a large package.
